subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Self-Healing Materials: Damage That Fixes Itself
description: A quick win: understand Self-Healing Materials: Damage That Fixes Itself.

hook.text: Cut a piece of self-healing polymer in half. Press the pieces together. They fuse back in minutes.

buildup.text: Some self-healing materials use microcapsules that burst when cracked, releasing a healing agent into the gap.

discovery.text: Others use reversible chemical bonds. Heat or light triggers the bonds to reform across the crack.

twist.text: Smartphone screens that heal scratches already exist in labs. The challenge is making them cheap enough to sell.

climax.text: Self-healing coatings on ships and pipelines could eliminate billions in corrosion maintenance costs.

quiz.question: How do microcapsule-based self-healing materials work?
options: Capsules absorb moisture from the air to fill cracks
Capsules burst when cracked and release a healing agent
Capsules generate heat that melts material around the damage
